item.content:encoded:

Here's some crit:

Central Narrative:

My main concern here is the execution of your narrative, you claim this is an SCP article, yet this appears to lean more towards being a tale. How is all this information portrayed in the article? Interviews, journals, casually in the description, where is it? You mention that there will be an interview but nothing about its contents.

clumsiness on the part of the retrieving agents has let the backpack claim them.

Are these not highly trained and briefed MTF Agents? They're not ones to simply inconveniently fuck up.

backpack is frequently found alone

I imagine a lot of these instances happen while the kid is hitchhiking and he suddenly bursts out bleeding in a car, or while working "odd jobs" or while riding the bus.

This:

even just grabbing the backpack is sufficient

Contradicts this:

Once someone finds and opens the backpack

And this:

Once opened the person opening it is transformed

Frankly, it seems like you have a generally good idea of the story but have no idea how you plan on presenting it in a digestible way to the reader. I'd like to see you expand on the execution side of things and fix some of the plot holes I pointed out.

item.title: Re: Nechronometer
item.content:encoded:
After some critique and conversation over on IRC, I'm giving this a greenlight. This has a lot of potential as both a tale and the start to a tale series. My main advice going forward would be to ensure that your main characters are well-developed, as that seems to be the focus of both this tale and the series at large.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Nechronometer

This one has a lot of issues, but lets start with the positive. I like the idea of a decomposed justice-loving Santa. But your execution leaves a lot to be desired.

Firstly, there are a couple of plot holes. There are probably millions of crimes committed in the month of December in just America alone. If this SCP showed up for every single one, the foundation would have a serious problem preventing the public from finding out about it. To fix this, perhaps you can change the article so that this scp only appears for extremely heinous crimes.

The same goes for instances where the scp shows up to give people presents. The scp showing up to give people presents could result in the public finding out about anomalies. The foundation needs a way to prevent the public from finding out, so either remove this bit or add a way for the scp foundation to track the scp so they can amnesticize individuals who were exposed.

The concepts also leaves a lot of unanswered questions. For instance, can the scp be in two places at once? If a bunch of people commit a crime at the same time but in different places, will the scp appear for only one person, or will a manifestation of the scp appear for all of the people.

Another question is if people have to "fix their unlawful act" for the scp to leave them alone, what counts as fixing an unlawful act. If you murdered someone, would you need to find a way to bring the person you murdered back to life. You need to create a specific set of rules that can be applied universally.

Additionally, you never specify what powers the scp has. Can it teleport? What if you try to fight it while the scp is trying to disembowel you. Does it have a way to immobilize its targets through combat or an afflicted paralysis? That needs to be specified.

Finally, why do people exposed to the scp need to be killed if any unlawful act can summon the scp? That seems excessive and inefficient, which is why the foundation wouldn't do it. It seems more likely that the foundation would investigate what those individuals did and determine and appropriate response. Additionally, why does the tree as well as the dishes/containers for the milk and cookies need to be incinerated. You said that was to prevent contamination, but I thought the scp only affected individuals who did unlawful acts. Is the scp diseased or something?

Overall, there are lots of unanswered questions and glaring plot holes.

There are also lots of issues with you grammar scattered throughout the article. I'm not going to list them all since this is already a long post, but one example is in the very first sentence, where you use "is" when you should use "are". There are several other mistakes like this throughout the article

You also have a bad habit of making your sentences to long by writing in a very indirect and convoluted way. For instance, you wrote:

"SCP 5655 will manifest nearby an individual who has committed an unlawful act in the duration of the month December."

The first issue is that you tend to use a conjugation of "is" before every verb in this sentence (manifest and commit). You shouldn't do that sparingly at most. It would be better like this:

"SCP 5655 manifests near individuals who commit unlawful acts in the duration of the month December."

Another way to cut down on fluff is at the very end of that sentence, where you wrote "in the duration of the month of December". That can be shortened to "during the month of December", giving us the final edited version of that sentence:

"SCP 5655 manifests near individuals who commit unlawful acts during the month December."

Writing it like this is clearer and more concise. Most of you sentences have issues like this, which makes the overall article sound unprofessional. That takes away from the immersion of the entry, since the foundation is supposed to be all about cold professionalism.

item.title: Box of Miscellaneous Items
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: no

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional i guess

Page Layout (Optional): Pictures, story, tabs for testing and the like.

Elevator Pitch: Additional Notes: Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.I have an idea, but not sure how good it is so I want some advice. The skip is legit a cardboard box of random items. Every person swears the box is anomalous. But nothing happens, no sensor readings, no properties, nothing. It is, for all purposes, a random box with random goods inside. Just a plain old box. Yet, the Foundation- in all their wisdom and favor- cannot accept that they might have gotten one wrong. So its classified as either keter since the foundation starts associating random mundane everyday bad luck with it just to make some sense of it.

Pretty much, I want to tell this story of the Foundation being so zealous and confident that they cannot accept that they made a single mistake somewhere and have been wasting time on an ordinary box.

Central Narrative: Its going to describe the long and turtourus experience of many researchers attempting to prove that this box is anomalous. From scanners to shoving the box in with other skips, to eventual word of mouth fear of the box and its supposed properties. Eventually with high clearance the story will be shown that more and more tests came back negative, until only the O-5 council access shows it is a normal box but the council cannot admit it was a mistake.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I want to tell the story not of the Foundation being perfect, but rather as a flawed machine that thinks its perfect. Of thinking they cannot even make a single mistake.

edit: format

item.title: A Canary In The Coal Mine
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Page Layout (Optional): It will begin with a standard SCP article structure, followed by a series of experiment logs, journal extracts and Foundation documents explaining the story of the discovery of the subject.

Elevator Pitch: One day a researcher discovers a strange correlation between co-worker drinking a specific brand of soda and disasters/containment breaches occuring to their projects which he is certain is a viable "warning-light" to help contain dangerous SCPs.

Central Narrative: An anonomous researcher in one of the foundation sites has been secretly classified as a thaumiel class SCP, used as an early warning system for potential disasters that may befall foundation projects. Should this researcher drink a can of soda of a brand they typically claim to hate, it is a sign that a project which the researcher is assigned to will have a some form of disaster occur to it.

One observant co-worker, Dr. Gables, notices this trend and begins documenting it. What follows is a series of test logs and journal extracts of Dr. Gables investigating this anomouly and putting the paperwork in to give the researcher an official SCP designation. As the logs go on, experiments ramp up and start getting strange. By the time Dr. Gables has orchestrated an entire breach event resulting in multiple deaths, we realise that he had been operating without foundation clearance the entire time.

He uses an edited version of his obervations (with his involvment having been removed) to get the researcher an official SCP designation. Following a few more experiments, Dr. Gables goes insane and assaults the researcher. Following this, the Foundation investigates Dr. Gables to find his original observations that proved his involvement in multiple incidents, as well as numorous logs documenting other Foundation personnel and a large amount of blackmail which he has been using to get away with his actions. This concludes with a notice of termination of Dr. Gables and the reassignment of the SCP project to another researcher.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The dynamics of the relationships between Foundation researchers as well as the covert workings of a researcher with their own agendas and goals.

Additional Notes: I'm scared that readers may lose interest before getting to the meat of the story which would take place in the experiment logs and other attached documents.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea - A house and its occupant
item.content:encoded:
I'll address these in order.
I swapped the order of the entities - XXXX-A is the woman, and XXXX-B is the house. Sorry for confusion.

+ show block
– hide block

1) Currently, diary entries describe how she summons things. She first figures out she has some anomalous properties after an interaction with a strange man who enters her house. When asked to find an object, she has an urge to reach forward and grab for it, upon which her hand enters a location not of this dimension. She can then grab the object and retrieve it. Isn't so much like a portal or some large wormhole that opens, but more similar to if you were to reach your hand into a pool of water, and the surface of the water was actually just in the air. (It isn't water, but its the same idea.)

2) I agree with you on the overused diary entries. I'll work on mixing them up with diary and interviews, but I don't want to bog down the article with multiple (possibly 4-5) interview collapsibles. I'm not sure if people want to read that.

3) See number 1.

4) Extent: she can summon any object upon request. Limitations: she has to be able to recognize what they are (not something vague, like the color purple), and she has to be inside whichever house is designated as XXXX-B.

5) I'm really not sure what to do here in terms of just XXXX-A exploring the dimension on her own. I want to start to introduce the Foundation more heavily around this point.

6) Will remove both joke and horror. I don't know what to categorize this SCP as, though.

7) See 4. Additionally, what I wish to define as an item that won't disappear is any item that is owned directly by either XXXX-A, her husband, or her children. Things such as furniture, a television, beds, microwave, etc, do not disappear. But if, say, XXXX-A's mother-in-law's cousin visits, and leaves her glasses in the house (XXXX-B), the glasses will disappear after some time.

8) I didn't word this properly. The description is written in a clinical, SCP-Researcher tone. There is a police report inserted in the Description section which contains an interview between a police officer and a burglar who broke into XXXX-A's house (XXXX-B).

9) I haven't gotten to the actual meat and potatoes of her introduction to the foundation yet. The Foundation will eventually obtain a copy of the police report and send a field agent to investigate, upon which the Foundation will respond with a bit more presence (possibly a supposed gas leak, evacuating nearby neighbors, leaving the Foundation free to inspect both the house and SCP-XXXX-A and her family for 'illness' or whatever happens when you're exposed to lots of natural gas.)

Thank you for your criticism. I'll make the appropriate changes.

item.title: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror (body horror)

Page Layout (Optional): Class, containment procedures, description, addenda (including a voiceover mp3 file with sound effects)

Elevator Pitch: Pregnant woman is found frozen in the arctic, torn in half, fetus missing. Top half of body is dead, lower half moves erratically on its own, possibly with a purpose or cognition.

Central Narrative: Corpse was found frozen in Yukon when villagers noticed a strange, unidentified creature moving erratically. Corpse's lower half is controlled by a series of live neurons that consume the bone and ligament tissue and shock the muscles into moving convulsively, allowing it to crawl. It will violently hyperextend its joints (bending knees backwards and such) and break its own bones to move. The live neuron DNA matches the dead woman, whose brain is somewhat shrunken, or possibly her fetus. Lead scientist believes it's capable of navigation and is searching for something, but regrets that its lifespan is so short as a result of consuming its own flesh and progressively deflating in size, that they'll never know what it wants. It must remain frozen to stay alive until the foundation finds a way to save it or find what it's looking for.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Using body horror as a focus, of which I haven't seen much here, and a full story with open-ended conclusion that is coherent with beginning, middle, and end if the reader reads between the lines. Specifically, I'd like to include a voiceover file from the scientist's observation session with written transcript, recording the skittering and cracking noises the skip makes, with a subtle hint/easter egg for readers to listen for, revealing what it's capable of, and possibly answering the question of what it actually wants (this won't be included in the transcript, so that the reader is left to think and interpret it on their own).

Additional Notes: Please advise how to include the mp3 file with submission, as it's essential to the storytelling, thanks.

How does this add anything to the story. Also, don't use "may" when giving your concept, does it or does it not?

explodes a goat fetus that will wreak havoc

Do you have anything to say that this isn't just "gore for the sake of gore"? To me it seems like this "exploding goat fetus" adds nothing to the story.

Central Narrative:

Speaking of the story, what exactly is it? The recovery by the MTF? The incident about the hunter getting into the site? These seem like B-Plots rather than some over-arching narrative that is generally required for successful articles.

I think my main issue with this is just that it seems a bit silly, a humanoid goat that explodes when killed and shoots out a flying fetus. Stranger things exist, but what is the reason that this one should?


JamaisJ, can you start refreshing the page in another tab or something before you post your crit? This is the second time you've posted crit minutes after me and reiterated the same points.

item.title: Re: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France
item.content:encoded:
SCP-8839-J is the 'light theme' for foundation messaging system 'SCiPNET'. Whatever entity or force of nature created SCP-8839 is, according to foundation analysis, in-human, and is likely more powerful and more evil than every other object in and out of containment, combined. SCP-8839-J is the most dangerous cognitohazard ever discovered, and as such is considered a "Class Φ Cognitohazrd"1, the only of its kind. According to the SCPF IT help desk "SCP-8839-J can be activated by clicking the Cognitohazard - Automatic Removal button on your SCiPNET terminal, scrolling to Cognitohazard - Automatic Removal and clicking the button 'light theme'".

Deleted at -15 and three votes.

SCP-5314 refers to 127 anomalous instances of Gallus Gallus domesticus of the ''Leghorn" race. SCP-5314 instances are sapient and demonstrate an ability to organize themselves as a society. All SCP-5314 instances follow the same religion and spend the majority of their time practicing it. Documents made by instances of SCP-5314 call it the ''Fellowship of the glorious egg''.

Deleted at -14 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

cybersqyd

+ show block
– hide block

The idea of the chickens effectively re-enacting the story of jesus isn't like, necessarily a bad idea here; but the execution feels…really lacking? The break-neck pace of the story telling and the complete lack of commentary on the story combine to mean this has no impact on me as a reader. Like, if this was making some kind of point about Christianity or the forming of religions as a whole, then maybe I could vibe with it. Alternatively, having some kinda unique spin on the story and really giving us a sense of charm towards the characters in the style of e.g. SCP-4693 could help kick this over the line.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight On My Idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy/Horror

Elevator Pitch: A Euclid SCP which creates instances of anomalous stone fountains in the yards of all integrated residents of a small, isolated township in Northern New Jersey. Memetic effects cause the population to consider the appearance and disappearance of these fountains as normal.

Central Narrative: The Foundation is in the process of investigating and researching this anomaly, but really no true containment is deemed necessary… so far. Researchers front as locals or vacationers to try and sneak past the defensive isolated population. Posing as an environmental group, they interview and interrogate locals on the appearance and disappearance of these fountains.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The memetic effects on the locals cause paranoia, defensiveness, and a stubborn attitude in regards to the fountains. This will be expanded upon in the interview logs, which I plan to have make up a lot of the page. Don't want to give TOO much away.

Additional Notes: I have already written a pretty in depth draft, just excluding the interview logs. Feel free to ask any questions, or to see the sandbox page.
